paper.title_en: Information entropy and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>-scaling law in central <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></math> <math><mo>+</mo></math> <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></math> collisions at 20–350 MeV/nucleon
paper.abstract_en: Within the isospin-dependent quantum molecular-dynamics (IQMD) framework, we investigate the multiplicity information entropy <math><mi>H</mi></math> of neutrons, protons, intermediate-mass fragments (IMFs), and all fragments, together with the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>-scaling behaviors, in central <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> collisions over an incident energy range of <math><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>350</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>nucleon</mi></mrow></math>. The information entropy of IMFs exhibits a plateau around <math><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>110</mn></mrow></math> MeV/nucleon, while that of all fragments shows a pronounced turning point at a similar energy. When considered together with other observables, these features reflect a correlated change in fragment production dynamics in this energy region. In contrast, the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>-scaling analysis of the largest fragment charge <math><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></math> does not indicate a transition from <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> to <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> over the same energy range. However, the charged-fragment multiplicity exhibits distinct <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>-scaling behaviors in low- <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>80</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>nucleon</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> and high-energy <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>350</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>nucleon</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> regions. These combined observations suggest that the multiplicity information entropy and the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>-scaling behavior of charged fragments consistently reflect a coherent change in the fragmentation dynamics around <math><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>110</mn></mrow></math> MeV/nucleon.
